current_episode.title: Aligning Investments with Climate Values: How Green Portfolio Empowers Everyday Investors

guest.bio_context: Bonnie Gurry holds undergraduate and graduate degrees in mechanical engineering and spent her early career building micro devices in clean rooms. Over time, she transitioned to the business side of climate technology, obtained an MBA, and worked at a financial software company where she recognized the intersection of climate and finance. This experience led her to found Green Portfolio after realizing her own investments were fueling the climate crisis despite her commitment to sustainability.

context.real_quote: Aligning your investments with climate goals can be 21 times more effective than pretty much all the lifestyle activities combined.

context.transcript_excerpt: I don't know if there are a lot of people that understand that when they're investing in mutual funds or things in the stock market, that they could be investing in some things that maybe don't align with their values. Welcome to the Angel Next Door podcast, your gateway to the dynamic world of angel investing. I'm your host, Marsha Dawood, and together we will demystify what it means to invest in early stage companies, who's behind it, and how anyone can be a part of it. If you've ever wondered how you can affect the change you want to see in the world, then tune in to learn more. In this episode, I'm talking to Bonnie Gurry, founder of Green Portfolio, who shares her unique journey from mechanical engineer to climate-focused fintech entrepreneur. We discuss how your money might be fueling the climate crisis without you even realizing it. We also talk about why aligning your investments with your values is now more accessible than ever, and how you can make a bigger impact through your portfolio than you can through any single lifestyle change. Bonnie also reveals eye-opening facts about the true power of banking decisions, the rise of sustainable financial advising, and what the coming great wealth transfer means for women and next-generation investors. Enjoy the show. Well, Bonnie, welcome to the Angel Next Door podcast. Thank you so much for having me. I appreciate it. It's great to be here and have this conversation. Yeah, I'm excited to hear all about green portfolio. So before we get started, tell us a little bit about your background and how you came to think, you know what, I really think there needs to be something like green portfolio in the world. Sure, I'm happy to. I started my adult life actually as a mechanical engineer. I have an undergrad and graduate degree in mechanical engineering. Spent much of my time in clean rooms actually building micro devices and things of this nature until I realized what I wanted to work on was solving this climate crisis. And a lot of the, especially 20 odd years ago, a lot of the advances that needed to be made were in the world of engineering and manufacturing and things of this nature. So that's really where I started putting my efforts was how could I, as a mechanical engineer at that time, start to build the kinds of products and services we needed to solve the climate crisis. And just over time, being in New York City, you end up in finance by bit. And over my career, even though I started out as an R&D engineer, I found myself working more and more on the business side, the business case of bringing a new technology to market or working on a project that would eventually earn a return. Ended up getting my MBA and this over time also I worked at a financial software company. I got to see more and more of the intersection of climate and finance, which are deeply intertwined. And and was just really frustrated. I was doing all of this and realizing that my investments, my money was sitting in accounts and investments that were fueling the climate crisis. Right. And that really didn't sit well with me. It was pretty frustrating that as a retail investor, it was hard to unwind myself from investments that did not match my values. and that's where I really started to dig into the different opportunities within the climate, finance, and fintech space. At the time, I actually was working at a small venture capital firm and was seeing some really interesting services come across my plate, but never saw the one I wanted, which was like, help me figure out how to align my investments, my children's inheritance with what matters to me. And that's really where Green Portfolio came from, was just trying to help people find climate aligned financial products and services that they can access, right? That you don't need to be extremely wealthy. So for many years, like if you, I don't know, had a family office or were an endowment or the state pension fund, they were doing these activities

If you bank with these large institutions, your money indirectly finances oil and gas exploration and drilling projects. Banks' scope three category 15 emissions are primarily related to their investment and lending activities.

pending_qa.r: Morgan Stanley and others have conducted longitudinal studies showing that sustainable funds have actually outperformed traditional funds on average.
